skill.name: sql-expert
skill.description: SQL assistance for writing queries, improving performance, designing schemas, planning migrations, and debugging database issues across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and SQL Server.
skill.summary: Write, optimize, and review SQL queries, schemas, indexes, and migrations.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Static warnings are almost entirely false positives from SQL examples, Markdown code fences, and benign Python dictionary usage. I found one real medium issue: helper functions interpolate SQL identifiers and clauses without validation. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Helper script builds SQL with raw identifiers and clauses.
remediation.suggestion: Validate table, column, join, and order inputs against an allowlist. Use SQLAlchemy identifier quoting and bind values through parameters.

content.value_statement: Database work often slows down when queries, indexes, and migrations are hard to reason about. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured SQL guidance for safer and faster database changes.
actual_capabilities: Drafts SELECT queries with joins, subqueries, CTEs, and window functions.
Explains query plans and recommends indexes for common performance issues.
Designs normalized schemas with keys, constraints, and relationship patterns.
Plans migrations with rollback steps and lower downtime patterns.
Provides examples for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and SQL Server syntax.
Includes a Python helper for schema inspection, query timing, and sample data generation.
limitations: It cannot access your database unless you provide tools, credentials, or query results.
Generated SQL must be tested against your exact engine version and schema.
Performance advice depends on real execution plans, table sizes, and index statistics.
The helper script should only receive trusted identifiers until validation is added.

use_cases.title: Build Reporting Queries
use_cases.description: Create clear analytical SQL with joins, grouping, filtering, and window functions for product or finance reports.

use_cases.title: Tune Application Queries
use_cases.description: Review slow queries, explain likely bottlenecks, and propose indexes or rewrites for production services.

use_cases.title: Plan Schema Changes
use_cases.description: Design tables, constraints, and migrations with rollback plans and lower risk deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Basic Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a SQL query for this goal: [goal]. Use these tables and columns: [schema]. Explain each clause briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this database schema for normalization, constraints, indexes, and naming. Suggest practical improvements for [database engine].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Slow Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this slow query and execution plan. Identify bottlenecks, propose indexes, and suggest a safer rewritten query.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for this schema change: [change]. Include rollout steps, rollback steps, data backfill, and verification checks.

output_examples.input: A slow customer orders report with repeated joins and missing filters.
output: Identifies the likely join and filtering bottlenecks.
Recommends targeted indexes for customer and order date lookups.
Suggests a clearer query shape and explains tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: A proposed user and subscription schema before launch.
output: Reviews relationships, keys, uniqueness rules, and nullable fields.
Flags missing constraints and ambiguous status handling.
Suggests migration and validation checks before production use.

output_examples.input: A request to add a required column to a large table.
output: Breaks the change into add, backfill, verify, and enforce phases.
Includes rollback considerations and low traffic execution guidance.
Lists checks for row counts, null values, and application compatibility.

best_practices: Provide the database engine, schema details, table sizes, and relevant indexes with each request.
Use execution plans and real timing data when asking for performance advice.
Test generated SQL in development before running it on production data.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for production migrations without rollback and verification requirements.
Do not accept broad SELECT statements when only a few columns are needed.
Do not pass untrusted table names or clauses into the helper script.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and SQL Server patterns. Some examples are engine specific.

faq.question: Can it inspect my live database?
faq.answer: Only if your environment provides database access. Otherwise it works from schemas, queries, and plans you provide.

faq.question: Does it write production ready migrations?
faq.answer: It can draft migration plans and SQL, but you should test them against backups and staging data first.

faq.question: Can it improve query performance?
faq.answer: Yes. Results are strongest when you include execution plans, row counts, existing indexes, and database version details.

faq.question: Does it prevent SQL injection?
faq.answer: It recommends parameterized queries and safe patterns, but your application code must enforce proper binding and validation.

faq.question: Does it replace a database administrator?
faq.answer: No. It supports analysis and drafting, while production approval should remain with qualified database owners.
